findings.description: A metered request that OpenRouter accepted but that then failed client-side (read timeout, connection reset, or a 'timed out' error that classifies as UNKNOWN) comes back with models_attempted set and no generation_id. _dispatch_metered then skips recording and leaves spend_recorded=None. The result is no ledger row, no spool entry, and no metered_spend_unrecorded degradation. Spend that may have been billed goes uncounted silently, and later budget rechecks use a total that is too low. The same gap applies to TRANSIENT 500/503 falls-through to the fallback model within one round.
findings.resolution: When models_attempted is non-empty and generation_id is absent after a transport exception, set spend_recorded=False (or emit a distinct 'metered_spend_unknown' degradation) so the round surfaces possible unrecorded spend; optionally spool a reservation-sized row.

findings.description: When the response has no usage.cost, row_from_review_result sends actual_usd=None (dropped by exclude_none). The server's LedgerService._ledger_row then computes _token_cost with no rates and gets 0.0 (float(rate or 0.0)). The stored row says tokens_estimated=true and actual_usd=0, so the coordinator ceiling, metered_usd_used and spooled_total_usd all count that call as free.
findings.resolution: Human decision on the estimate source for cost-less responses: reservation amount, catalog per-token rates, or refuse/flag. Any of these beats silently recording $0.

findings.description: The _oneshot_spend_context docstring says archived changes are included, but an output dir of openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-21-<id>/reviews gives change_id='2026-10-21-<id>'. The consequences are a wrong work_unit_ref, and spend_recorder's _change_dir finding neither a live nor an archive (*-<id>) match. Spooling would then create a stray openspec/changes/2026-10-21-<id>/reviews/spend-spool.jsonl tree.
findings.resolution: When parts[-3] == 'archive', strip the leading YYYY-MM-DD- prefix from parts[-2] (or resolve via the shared openspec_paths helper); add a test for the archived path.

findings.description: _extract_content calls choices[0].get(...) without checking that choices[0] is a dict. A malformed or proxy-mangled 200 response, such as choices: ["..."] or [null], raises AttributeError. The exception escapes dispatch instead of becoming a classified ReviewResult failure, so the lane crashes rather than degrading cleanly.
findings.resolution: Guard with isinstance(choices[0], dict) (and message dict) and return None so the existing empty-content path classifies the failure.

findings.description: The duplicate_model_family check in select_reviewers looks only at the primary adapter.model. Fallback models go through the anthropic-family rejection in from_config_dict but not through the duplicate-family check. A fallback from a family already served (for example openai/...) could therefore be dispatched after a CAPACITY fallback, which would defeat D2 independence. The current archetypes.yaml fallbacks are all qwen, so this does not happen today.
findings.resolution: Accept for now; consider checking every model in the fallback chain against selected families when configs grow.

findings.description: can_dispatch no longer checks for api_key_env. A pi/CLI lane with OPENROUTER_API_KEY unset is now counted as available, and passes --check-vendors through 'pi --version'. It can therefore fill a fill_target slot and then fail with AUTH at dispatch time. This matches design D1 (honest dispatch-time auth failure, classified as capability_unavailable), so it is not a defect; it is noted here as a behaviour change.

CompositeOrchestrator gives the inner ReviewOrchestrator include_lanes=others and caller_vendors=(LANE,) but no exclude_vendor. Inner selection can count the claude_code CLI toward fill_target before include_lanes filters it out. On the intended cloud path (claude_code is the only CLI) countable stays at 1, so the metered lane is still selected and the behaviour is correct. Passing exclude_vendor=LANE would make this explicit.
